lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_asteria: Asteria, the world of two moons
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_asteria.te:
The world you woke up in is called Asteria. Three realms share its lands — Aldoria, Sahra and Nordheim — and everywhere lie the ruins of an older empire, Velmora.

The air here holds something your world never had: mana. And in the sky, two pale moons fade at dawn.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_mana.text:
Mana is the blood of the world. They say everything in Asteria — people, monsters, stone and wind — is woven from it, and that all of it flows from a single origin.

Mages spend Mana; warriors call the same force Vigor; marksmen call it Focus. Three ways for the same blood to run.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_glyphs.tex:
Nobody here is born knowing ready-made spells: magic is WRITTEN. Glyphs are the grammar of mana — a Form says how the spell comes out, Effects say what it does, Augments change the manner, and Laws rule inside a Domain.

The Grimoire is the notebook. The rest is creativity.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_elements.t:
Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Light and Shadow. Six shrines keep the essence of each, and only the worthy pass their trials. Arcane is mana without color.

Elements can fuse — Magma, Ice, Twilight... The old mages called that heresy. The summoned call it Tuesday.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_circles.te:
Every ten levels the soul hits an invisible ceiling. Only the Ascension Ritual breaks it, and it has a price: facing your own Shadow.

A native who reaches the Third Circle is a respected mage; the Fifth, a legend. Nobody understands why the summoned never stop climbing.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_moons.text:
The old silver moon was always there; the elves say it guides their arrows. The second, pale and smaller, appeared in a single night a little over a thousand years ago.

The Church of the Dawn calls it a gift. The skalds of Nordheim call it an eye. Nobody knows for sure.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_summoned.t:
From time to time someone wakes in this world having come from another — without mana, without a past, and growing far too fast. The natives call them the summoned: walking legends to some, walking trouble to others.

They all tell the same story: a gentle voice saying they were brought here for a reason. The body is new, made of this world's mana — which is why each summoned chooses their own race.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.world_souls.text:
When a native dies, the soul follows the cycle: light ones rise to the Celestial Sanctuary, heavy ones sink into the Abyss, and those that lose their heart become Hollows in the white desert of the Hollow World.

Shinigami guide souls; Quincy destroy Hollows; Necromancers meddle with the cycle on their own. The summoned stand OUTSIDE the cycle — near death, they become a soul and may return.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.history_dragon.t:
Before the shrines, before the Guardians and even before the two moons, there was a dragon that was every element at once. It introduces itself as “the origin of all magic”.

The first peoples learned to write its mana in glyphs. It slept. While it slept, all was well.
More than a thousand years ago a single empire covered the continent. Velmora raised towers, stone chambers and schools of glyphs; the ruins you find around the world are its remains.

Six great mages served at court. People remember them as the Six Sages. Of the empire, they only remember that it fell in one night.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.history_sages.te:
Pyra of Fire, a smith. Nerida of Water, a healer. Brom of Earth, a master builder. Aelis of Wind, a wanderer. Solen of Light, a priest. Nyra of Shadow, a spy.

From them came the dwarves' rune forge, the witches' recipes, the towers, the Guild, the Church of the Dawn and — so gossip says — the Underworld. The disciples of the six founded the Arcane Academy.
When the Dragon began to wake, the Six Sages could not kill it: only seal it beyond the Twilight. Its essence was split among six shrines, one per element, and a jailer was left on watch.

That same night, the second moon appeared in the sky.
A thousand years ago the world cracked. The Abyss sank, the Celestial Sanctuary rose, a wound of mingled Light and Shadow opened in the middle of the ocean — the Twilight Rift — and Velmora fell in one night.

The blame lies with the Twilight Herald, who summoned the first hero from another world... and devoured him. The realms count their years from that night.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.history_ashen.te:
After the Rupture came two hundred years of hunger and monsters. Goblins, orcs and kobolds banded into the Horde. The dwarves went down and shut the door.

From the survivors three realms were born: Aldoria in the southern fields, Sahra over the dunes that buried the east, Nordheim with the soldiers stranded in the snow. The Guild, the Church and the Academy date from then.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.history_demon_ki:
In the Nether stands a citadel of black stone, and in it a lord of demons who fights like a court swordsman — until he tires of pretending. The people call him the Demon King; the demons call him Lord.

He does not attack the world. He stays there, repeating that it is “still his”. Aldoria is the realm he hates most, and nobody can say why.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.history_now.text:
Today is the year one thousand after the Rupture. Ancient beasts have woken, the second moon looks paler, and the Twilight Rift pulses.

And suddenly, instead of one summoned per generation, several appeared at once. You are one of them.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.realm_aldoria.te:
The human heart of the continent: golden fields, walled cities, villages and the Lord in the capital. They say the king was once an adventurer.

Aldoria stays out of the quarrel between Sahra and Nordheim — for now. Work, law and heroes who pay for their own drinks are valued here. Demons are looked at with suspicion.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.realm_sahra.text:
Sandstone cities, caravans, oases and the Sultan. Sahra measures time by the dunes, not by kings — and beneath the dunes whole provinces of Velmora lie sleeping.

It sells gold and spices, wants northern iron cheap, and respects those with dragon blood.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.realm_nordheim.t:
Fortresses of stone and timber, mead halls, wolves and the Jarl. Nordheim bows neither to cold nor to monsters.

Its people descend from the legionaries stranded in the north when the empire fell. They sell iron, and the skalds sing of heroes for a thousand winters.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.faction_guild.te:
The Guild does not care whether you are a legend or trouble: it wants your name on the register and work well done. Every summoned worth the name starts with an F-rank card and a smiling receptionist.

They say it began with the wanderers who followed Aelis, the Sage of Wind, who never had a home.
The scholars of magic: theses, Trials and the grammar of glyphs. It was founded by the disciples of the Six Sages so that nothing they knew would be lost.

A good deal was lost anyway. And now and then the Academy expels someone for “forbidden research” — the Renegade Archmage took an entire tower.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.faction_church.t:
“The Dawn always returns.” The priests heal, purify and hunt the undead, following the teachings of Solen, the Sage of Light.

The Church does not forgive those who meddle with the cycle of souls, and is the declared rival of the Underworld.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.faction_underwor:
Thieves, fences and night contracts. Help the Underworld and you lose the trust of Church and Kingdom.

The old hands swear the organization was born from something nobler: the eyes and ears of Nyra, the Sage of Shadow, who kept watch over something. What they watched, nobody remembers.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.faction_wildfolk:
Fairies and nature spirits, older than Velmora. Protect the forest and they leave you alone.

Their home is the Fey Realm: hills under a twilight that never ends, glowing mushrooms and laughter that comes from nowhere.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.faction_horde.te:
Clans of goblins, orcs and kobolds, natural enemies of the realms. They banded together in the Ashen Years and never truly parted.

When a chief falls — the Goblin King, the Orc Lord, the Kobold Lord — the others smell fear and decide to show who is in charge.
They say the dwarves never left: they only went deeper than anyone dared to dig. Far below the deepslate there are stone halls no map shows.

Mithril is still forged there and runes are still carved — an art they learned from Pyra. Dwarves never forget a good customer. Or a bad one.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_nether.text:
The underground of fire. To the realms it is merely where fortresses and quartz come from; to demons, it is home.

This is where the Demon Citadel stands, with the Infernal Forge and the Pact Altar.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_end.text:
What was left outside when the world cracked: islands floating over nothing. Beyond the Ender Dragon, on the outer islands, stands a tower of shelves — the Library of the Void.

Hooded scribes still copy books nobody reads, and the tomes keep the grammar of space itself.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_elemental_pl:
Beyond the sky lies an impossible archipelago: the Ember Isles, the Suspended Sea, the Earthen Peaks and the Storm Skies. The four Elemental Guardians reign there.

You enter through the Elemental Gate, a stone circle with four obelisks — after the Third Circle.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_abyss.text:
Below the world, the Abyss beats like a black heart. Darkness has weight there, and the eyes watching from the Void never blink.

It is where heavy souls sink, and where pacts come from. The Sovereign rules from a throne made of dead stars.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_celestial.te:
Above the clouds, crystal cities over gardens of cloud, guarded by angels who tolerate no intruders.

It is where light souls rise. The six-winged Seraph watches over it all, absolutely convinced that order is worth more than freedom.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_fey.text:
Hills under a twilight that never ends. You enter through a Fairy Ring — a circle of mushrooms and stones in the forest.

Beware the giggling. And the Thorn Queen.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_hollow.text:
There is a tear in the sky that only opens at night. On the other side, a desert of white sand under a moon that never sets, quartz trees and bones the size of towers.

The Hollows live there — souls that lost their hearts and wear masks of bone — and, in Las Noches, those who rule their hunger.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_twilight.tex:
A wound in the fabric of the world, where Light and Shadow mingle into something that should not exist. On the other side time does not pass: there is only eternal twilight and an arena waiting for you.

The Rift only lets through those who defeated the Abyss Sovereign and the Seraph.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_trials.text:
The Trial Chambers lie outside the world: a silent hall, an altar, and beyond it an arena where your element tests whether you are worthy of it.

Nobody knows who built them. Every mage who wants to grow in an element walks through those doors one day.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_inner.text:
Silence, slow breathing and the sword on your lap: behind closed eyes lies a whole world. It is the Shinigami's soul, and the spirit of the Zanpakutō lives there.

Sometimes it wants to talk. Sometimes it wants to fight.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_endless_abys:
The bottom of the bottom. Everything ever defeated leaves an echo, and the echoes drain down there: endless floors, waves of creatures and the Shadows of bosses you have already beaten — stronger and darker.

Only those past level 100 can endure the descent.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.dim_home.text:
A pocket of space all your own, with a small house ready and room to build. There are no monsters or fights inside.

The magic that folds space this way is the same as in the tomes of the Library of the Void. The Home Key is expensive — ask at an inn.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_human.text:
Versatile and stubborn, humans adapt to any path. They were the people of Velmora and are the people of the three realms.

Every legend of this world began with a human who refused to give up.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_elf.text:
Children of the ancient forests — they were there before the empire. Keen senses, flawless aim, eyes that see in the dark.

They say the old moon guides their arrows.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_dwarf.text:
Short, sturdy and stubborn as rock. Born miners and masters of the forge, they see in the depths and laugh at poisons.

Most went below at the Rupture; the ones you see on the surface are the curious ones.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_half_orc.te:
Blood of the Horde and of men, children of the Ashen Years. Strong, feared and hard to bring down.

When the fury lights, nothing stops them.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_beastfolk.t:
Half person, half beast: alert ears, restless tail, a hunter's nose and a predator's leap.

They are the finest scouts of Nordheim and of the savannas of Sahra.
Descendants of dragon blood, with horns, tail, scales in the color of their ancestral element and a devastating breath.

In Sahra they are treated with respect — the desert remembers dragons.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_demon.text:
Marked by an ancient pact, they bear horns, a tail, wings of shadow and the fire of the Abyss in their veins. Charming... and dangerous.

None of them signed anything: the mark is inherited. Aldoria is wary all the same.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_angel.text:
Children of the sky with a golden halo and small feathered wings. They descend from those who came down from the Celestial Sanctuary.

Their holy light heals allies and burns the undead.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_phantom.tex:
A soul that came back from the cycle with a body of mist: half translucent, light as wind, seeing in the dark and letting blows pass through.

The Church of the Dawn is not quite sure what to do with them.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_arachnid.te:
Cave hunters with extra eyes and thin legs on their backs. They climb walls, weave webs and bite with venom.

Neighbors — and rivals — of the dwarves down below.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.race_slime.text:
Clotted mana that one day woke up. A body of translucent jelly that regenerates, bounces and swallows almost anything.

Underestimated... until it becomes king.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_mage.text:
The Mage neither prays nor bargains: he studies. At the Research Table every thesis is a problem of mana, and every thesis defended becomes a new glyph.

It is the way of the Arcane Academy. A mage is measured by the size of his vocabulary.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_witch.text:
The Witch does not ask for power: she cooks. Herbs, essences and the eyes of things you would rather not know become recipes in the cauldron.

The oldest recipes come from the notebooks of Nerida, the Sage of Water — the one that heals and the one that curses.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_warlock.te:
The Warlock draws the circle in chalk, lights the candles and calls someone from the other side. Patrons charge dearly, but pay better.

Demons recognize a Warlock from afar: he reads the same fine print they do.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_druid.text:
The Druid plants his own magic. The Ancestral Sapling grows with offerings and care, and each stage of the tree is an animal spirit and a piece of the world's heart.

It is the way of the Wildfolk. Whoever plants a forest never walks alone.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_necromance:
The Necromancer reaps what others leave behind: souls on the scythe, bones on the altar and, at midnight, the Ossuary Rite.

He meddles with the cycle of souls on his own. The Lich of the Forgotten Crypt is the example of one who did not know when to stop.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_smith.text:
Between hammer and anvil, the metal listens. The Smith does not buy weapons: he talks to the steel until it is born.

Every blow on the anvil is a glyph — the art of runes, which Pyra taught the dwarves.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_rogue.text:
Everything in this world has an owner — even spells. The Rogue disagrees. Pockets, mana, blessings and the spell just cast at you: it all fits in the Ledger.

The Underworld welcomes him with open arms (and an eye on its own pockets).
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_knight.tex:
The rune blade keeps spells the way a scabbard keeps steel. Five Oaths at the Altar turn the squire into a Knight King.

The legendary swords — from Caliburn's stone to the lake where the true one sleeps — are relics of the legions of Velmora.
Strength, haste, aegis, vitality: the Enchanter writes power onto himself and his allies as one writes in a book.

He keeps two forbidden pages — Anti-Magic and Heavenly Restriction. The art of Inscription comes from the scribes of the old empire.
Your sword has a name — you just have not heard it yet. In meditation the Shinigami descends to the Inner World, where the spirit of the blade waits.

Sealed, Shikai, Bankai: each release is a promise between soul and steel. Their trade is guiding souls and purifying Hollows.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_quincy.tex:
A Quincy does not create energy: he gathers it — from the air, from projectiles, from spells flying at him — and returns it as arrows.

They have hunted Hollows for generations, and they do not purify: they destroy. That is why they do not get along with the Shinigami.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_gunslinger:
Your mana comes out neither as lightning nor as flame: it comes out of the barrel. Every gun is made of mana, and every bullet carries the spell you build.

No native would have invented this. It was the idea of earlier summoned.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_ranger.tex:
The Ranger never hunts alone: the eagle marks the target, the wolf brings it down, the steed carries you away. And every arrow is built like a spell.

The Trail runs from Scout to Lord of Beasts — a tradition of the scouts of Nordheim.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.class_gambler.te:
Every Gambler spell rolls the dice: from −99% to +100% power. Bad luck exists — but Tension rises with every bad roll, and when the JACKPOT comes, luck becomes infinite.

The House always wins... unless you are the House.
A spinning steel ball is not a thrown stone: it is a lesson in geometry. Master Rotari teaches the Spin in five lessons.

Nine Parts of the Holy Corpse lie hidden in tombs around the world. They say the Saint, too, came from far away.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_horde.text:
The Goblin King counts stolen coins in a palisade fortress and swears the crown is his by right. The Orc Lord has never lost a duel. The Kobold Lord guards the summit of the Towers.

When one falls, the others decide to show who is in charge.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_minotaur.te:
In a labyrinth that shifts its place, the Minotaur counts the steps of whoever enters. Inside you cannot build, break or climb over walls.

There is only you, the corridors and his snorting, closer every time.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_dark_master:
In a crypt, a Lich keeps his own soul in a phylactery. On a profane altar, a chained Patron whispers pacts. In the swamp, a witch traded her soul for a bottomless cauldron. In a tower, an expelled Archmage smiles with all his illusions.

Not every power in this world was born clean.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_horrors.tex:
Some monsters roar and some monsters wait. The False Hydra sings a song that erases memory. The Mimic King turned every chest into a stomach. The Manticore hunts with a tail of spines.

They grew in the leftovers of the Rupture, where nobody was looking.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_titans.text:
Four beasts as old as the shrines: the Swamp Hydra, the Desert Basilisk, the Ruin Colossus and the Wyvern King of the Peaks.

They slept beneath the world. They say the rise of a summoned wakes them. The Colossus still guards a city that no longer exists.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_worm_king: The Worm King of the Depths
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_worm_king.t:
At the bottom of the Layered Dungeon sleeps a worm the size of a tower. It devours mana geodes — the crystals grew on its own carapace.

It vanishes into the earth and erupts beneath its prey.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_guardians.t:
Ignis in the Ember Isles, Tide in the Suspended Sea, the Primordial Golem in the Earthen Peaks and Zephyr in the Storm Skies.

They are old enough to remember who sealed the shrines. Whoever defeats all four is remembered as “the one who came from afar”.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_sovereign.t:
He rules the Abyss from a throne of dead stars, wearing a crown of horns. He is the one who signs on the other side of every pact.

He believes the summoned is the key to ending the war against the sky.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_seraph.text:
Six wings, a thousand eyes and the absolute conviction that order is worth more than freedom. He guards the Celestial Sanctuary.

He believes — like his enemy — that the summoned is the key to ending the war.
Barragan Louisenbairn, God-King of the Hollow World: crown of bone, axe of ash and the aspect of Old Age. The Sand Empress, whom every grain obeys like a blade.

And the Arrancar — Hollows who tore off their own mask and gained a name and pride.
Master of the Demon Citadel. He starts as a court swordsman — wide cut, thrust, flawless stance. Then he calls the Legion. And at the end he shouts that he is done pretending to be human.

His last words are always the same: “This citadel... is still... mine...”
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_star_devour:
In the Observatory, atop the Library of the Void, something huge sleeps gazing at the stars — and eating them.

It eats stars. You look like one.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_herald.text:
The cause of the Great Rupture. A thousand years ago he summoned the first hero from another world... and devoured him. He expands his own Domain, stops time and, exactly once, turns it back.

“You who were summoned from another world... have you come to see the end of this one?”
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.boss_dragon.text:
The dragon that was every element before the elements had names. Sealed beyond the Twilight by the Six Sages, it wakes when the Herald falls — and remembers everyone who bound it.

It does not fight a hero: it fights an army. And it returns. It always returns.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_towers.tex:
It is not true that “nobody knows” who raised the Challenge Towers and the Trial Chambers. It was Brom, the Sage of Earth, with Velmora's Order of Trials.

He knew that one day someone would come from outside, with no ceiling on their soul and no time to learn slowly. The towers are a training ground left for that person. The sign on the door — “Win or go back” — is a message for you.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_seventh.te:
The Sages were not six. There was an apprentice, the youngest, the one who wrote everything down: Vesper. He wrote the rite of the Call, and he agreed to stand between Light and Shadow holding the seal “for a few years”.

Nobody came back to relieve him. The Twilight Herald is not a monster the Sages fought. He is one of them — the one left behind.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_king.text:
The Demon King has a human name: Aldric Velmor, last Emperor of Velmora. On the night of the Rupture, with the capital falling, he signed the first pact with the Abyss — his whole court in exchange for never dying. The Abyss honored it to the letter.

His sister, Aldora, refused. She led the survivors to the southern fields and founded a kingdom bearing her own name: Aldoria. That is why he says everything is “still his”. And that is why he hates those golden fields so much.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_call.text:
Everything born in Asteria is made of the Dragon's mana — and nothing made of it can destroy it. So the Sages created the Call: a rite that pulls a soul from a world WITHOUT mana. An empty vessel. No ceiling. Able to break Circle after Circle, and to wound the origin.

The gentle voice you heard is their echo, hoping. But the Herald uses the same rite as a trap: he waits for each summoned to fill up to the Ninth Circle... and calls them to dinner. You were brought to finish the Sages' work. He thinks you were brought for him.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_beasts.tex:
The Hydra, the Basilisk, the Colossus and the Wyvern King are not just old beasts. They are pieces of the Dragon's sleep that slipped past the seal — dreams with teeth.

They wake when someone in the world grows too strong, because the Dragon, asleep, can feel it. Every Titan you bring down is the Dragon stirring in its bed.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_moon.text:
The pale moon is neither a gift nor an eye. It is the seal — seen from below. The Sages hung it in the sky on the night of the Sealing, and the Herald holds it from inside the Twilight.

That is why it looks weaker every century. When the second moon cracks, the Dragon wakes.
lore.isekai_mahou.entry.truth_dwarves.te:
The dwarves did not flee the Rupture. Pyra, the Sage of Fire, asked them to keep, deep down, the one thing she could not hide on the surface: the forge where the runes of the seal were carved.

They shut the door and have waited a thousand years for someone who knows how to ask the right way. A rune is not an ornament. It is a promise carved in metal.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_1.text:
“Year 461 of the Empire. Master Brom ordered yet another tower raised, and once again would not say for whom. Seven floors, a guardian at the top and a sign on the south door. When I asked who would train there, he answered: someone not yet born in this world.”

The chronicle describes the way to one of those towers.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_2.text:
“Our best mages stop at the Fifth Circle. It is not laziness: the soul presses against something and cannot pass. The Sages built sanctums to break that ceiling by force, with a core, four pedestals and a great deal of courage.”

In the margin, someone drew the way to an Ascension Sanctum.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_3.text:
“To guard the city of Varen they raised a golem the size of a tower and gave it a single order: none shall pass. Varen no longer exists. Nobody had the heart to tell it.”

The text ends with the direction of the ruins where it still stands guard.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_4.text:
“Here it was taught that a spell is a sentence: Form, Effect, Augment. Students who got the grammar wrong blew off their own eyebrows. Those who got it right blew off other people's.”

The page is what is left of a freshman guide, with a map to the Arcane Ruins.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_5.text:
“His Majesty had a stone labyrinth planted in the gardens and the champion of the guard set loose in it, so that no assassin would reach the palace. The palace fell. The labyrinth did not. Neither did the champion — he has merely changed a great deal.”

The back of the page shows where the labyrinth ended up.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.velmora_6.text:
“The sky cracked over the sea at sunset. Light and shadow mingled, like milk in ink. The capital sank before midnight. I write this in a boat, and the island behind me was not there yesterday.”

It is the last record of Velmora. It gives the island's position.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_1.text: “I kept Fire in a shrine and my forge somewhere else, far deeper. The dwarves swore silence. If you are reading this and know how to hold a hammer, go to the shrine first: Fire likes to know who is calling it.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_2.text: “Water heals and Water drowns, and both are the same recipe in different doses. I left the shrine near where it runs. My students will fight over the notebooks. Let them — just never let one of them keep them all.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_3.text: “Stone does not lie. I built the Earth shrine, the chambers and the towers by the same rule: whoever enters must leave stronger or not leave. It is not cruelty. Those who come after us will not have time to learn slowly.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_4.text: “I never had a home, so I left the Wind in a high place and my voice inside the rite. If someone is ever pulled here without asking, I want the first thing they hear to be kind. Sorry about that, by the way. Truly.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_5.text: “I told my people that the Dawn always returns. I did not tell them that I hung the seal in the sky and that it looks like a moon. A priest, too, chooses what he teaches. The Light shrine stands where the sun strikes first.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.sages_6.text: “We are six in the portrait and seven at the table. The boy asked to stand guard and none of us had the courage to say no. I left my shadows watching his door. If they forget what they watch, the fault is mine. The Shadow shrine stands where nobody looks twice.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.demon_1.text:
“A creditor of the Abyss was bound to an altar with four chains. It was the spy of my court who bound him. I read his contract before writing mine. I should have read it twice.”

The confession tells where the altar still stands.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.demon_2.text:
“I went down through the chasm with the crown on my head and the capital burning behind me. I asked for one thing only: that none of us would die that night. Down there someone smiled and said that was easy.”

He describes the descent — an Abyssal Chasm.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.demon_3.text:
“I raised the citadel on the same plan as the palace. Same throne room, same guard, same banners — only the stone changed. My courtiers have horns now. I still wear the gloves.”

The page gives the way, in the Nether, to the Demon Citadel.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.demon_4.text: “Before going down I buried what belonged to Aldric and not to a king of demons: my mother's ring, some coins with my face as a boy, trifles. My sister never knew where. If you find it, keep it. Just do not tell me.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.herald_1.text:
“Letter one. I woke in a field, with two moons in the sky and a voice saying I had been brought for a reason. I thought it was a dream. Then a slime bit me.

An old man showed me a stone circle with four obelisks and said the answer lay beyond it.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.herald_2.text:
“Letter two. There are two voices, not one. The first is kind and apologizes. The second only speaks when I grow stronger, and says my name like someone reading a menu.

The angels of the stairway say they hear neither.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.herald_3.text:
“Letter three. I asked a necromancer why the people here stop growing and I do not. He laughed and said their souls have an owner. Mine, it seems, came without a label.

He lives in a crypt and takes no visitors. He took me.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.herald_4.text:
“Letter four. The fairies are older than the empire and do not like to lie, only to laugh. I asked who called me. They stopped laughing.

They said: the twilight boy is hungry. And they sent me out of the ring.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.herald_5.text:
“Last letter. I cross the Rift tomorrow; I reached the Ninth Circle and the second voice never stops now. If I do not return, do not trust the invitation.

I buried what I will not need in there. It is yours. Go stronger than I went — and do not go alone.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_1.text:
“Cut off one head and two grow back. I lost three spears learning that. The stump has to burn — fire, always fire.

I noted where the lair is. I am not going back without a mage.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_2.text:
“He reigns over mountains and storms. Lightning falls where he points. I climbed with hemp rope; come down with rope that does not conduct.

The nest is on the marked peak.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_3.text:
“In the tomb beneath the dunes, statues of adventurers still hold their swords aloft. They are not statues. Do not meet his eyes; fight by reflection or from behind.

The entrance to the tomb is marked.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_4.text:
“A lion's body, bat wings and a tail that fires spines like a siege crossbow. The roar freezes your courage; cover your ears and keep walking.

The den is in the ravine I drew.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_5.text:
“I passed through an empty village and do not remember passing. It is in my notebook, in my handwriting: DO NOT LISTEN TO THE SONG. The heads only exist when nobody is looking.

I left the place marked. I think it was me.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.hunter_6.text:
“A vault full of chests, all unlocked. Too good to be true — and that is exactly it. Throw a stone at each chest before opening. If the stone vanishes, run.

The vault is where I marked. I warned you.”
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.smuggler_1.text:
“Rule one of the trade: never keep your profit where you sleep. I buried the first share far from the walls, deep enough that the cattle would not find it.”

The map is crude, but the X is clear.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.smuggler_2.text:
“The guards of Aldoria take bribes. Those of Nordheim take mead. Those of Sahra take both and arrest you anyway. This share stayed along the escape route.”

Another X, in another direction.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.smuggler_3.text:
“The Underworld charges ten percent of everything that passes through its hands. What does not pass through its hands, it does not charge. Hence this hole.”

The third X is circled twice.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.smuggler_4.text:
“If you are reading this, I have either retired or been arrested. Either way, I will not be needing it. Have a drink for me at an inn — and pay for your own.”

The last X, and a wine stain.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.deep_1.text:
The runes read: “We shut the door but did not lower the gate. Whoever digs their way here deserves at least a mug. Bring good iron and better manners.”

Below, an arrow points down — and sideways.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.deep_2.text:
The runes read: “Survey shaft number nine. Four floors opened, traps set, something big eating the geodes below. Sealed by order of the king. Those who go down do not always come up.”

The stone points to the ruin with the shaft.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.deep_3.text:
The runes read: “The kobolds have dug above us again. They steal pickaxes, sing badly and swear they have a king in a tower. Do not feed them.”

Someone scratched a map to the den.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.void_1.text:
“At night, with the right offering, the sky tears like black paper,
and on the other side the moon does not set.
Those who lost their heart walk the white sand.
Those who still have one, hold it with both hands.”

The song speaks of an altar of bone in the middle of nowhere.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.void_2.text:
“We copy the books nobody reads,
for space has a grammar and someone must remember it.
At the top, the reader sleeps and chews on stars.
Do not wake it. Or wake it, and bring friends.”

The song comes from the outer islands of the End.
lore.isekai_mahou.frag.void_3.text:
“I watched the second moon through the lens for forty nights.
It does not turn. It has no craters. It has seams.
On the fortieth night, a seam came open.
I burned my notes. This one escaped.”

The page came from a mage's tower.
